## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

SensorPermissionSystemImpl.openAppSettings — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/permission/SensorPermissionSystemImpl.kt:105-111

## Trigger

The user tapping the call-to-action that opens the system settings screen from the sensor or connectivity permission screen, after a permanent refusal — observed

## Today

`SensorPermissionSystemImpl.openAppSettings()` (`:105-111`) builds an
`Intent(Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS, ...)` and calls
`activity.startActivity(intent)` directly. Nothing checks beforehand
that an activity exists to resolve this intent — no
`resolveActivity`, no `queryIntentActivities`, no `try`/`catch` around
the call. On a device or OS version where the application-details
settings screen is absent, `startActivity` throws
`ActivityNotFoundException`, uncaught, on the activity's own thread.

`ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.openAppSettings()`
(`core-platform/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/platform/connectivity/permission/ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.kt:73-79`)
repeats the identical shape: the same `Intent`, the same unguarded
`activity.startActivity(intent)`, the same absence of a resolvability
check. Both are reached from `ActivityBoundPermissionHost`
(`app-wear` and `app-phone`), which calls `openAppSettings()` on the
permission system it wraps without any guard of its own.

## Expected

`openAppSettings()` resolves the settings `Intent` before launching
it — through the package manager, or by catching
`ActivityNotFoundException` around the `startActivity` call — and
treats an unresolvable intent as a nominal outcome: the call returns
without navigating away, the current permission screen stays
displayed, and the user is left with an indication of what to do by
hand rather than a crash. The same fix applies to both occurrences —
`SensorPermissionSystemImpl.openAppSettings()` and
`ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.openAppSettings()` — since neither
follows from the other and each throws independently.
